# Lab 10.6: Object Tables for Unstructured Data

## What We Are Going to Do
Create an object table over image files in Cloud Storage and query the file metadata with SQL.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] Create the object table.** Replace `YOUR_PROJECT`.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE EXTERNAL TABLE lab10.pet_images
WITH CONNECTION `YOUR_PROJECT.us.lab_conn`
OPTIONS (
  object_metadata = 'SIMPLE',
  uris = ['gs://cloud-samples-data/bigquery/tutorials/cymbal-pets/images/*.png'],
  max_staleness = INTERVAL 1 DAY,
  metadata_cache_mode = 'MANUAL'
);</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[SQL] Query the files as rows.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT uri, content_type, size, updated
FROM lab10.pet_images
ORDER BY size DESC
LIMIT 10;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Get a signed URL to view a file.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">SELECT uri, OBJ.GET_ACCESS_URL(ref, 'r').access_urls.read_url AS view_url
FROM lab10.pet_images LIMIT 3;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


   Open a `view_url` in your browser. The link expires after a few hours.

4. **[CLI] Refresh the file list.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">bq query --use_legacy_sql=false "CALL BQ.REFRESH_EXTERNAL_METADATA_CACHE('lab10.pet_images')"
bq show --schema lab10.pet_images</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


5. **[Console] Look at the schema.** Open `pet_images → Schema`. Every object table has the same columns: `uri`, `generation`, `content_type`, `size`, `md5_hash`, `updated`, `metadata` and `ref`.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Rows | One per file |
| Columns | Fixed metadata schema plus `ref` |
| Signed URL | `OBJ.GET_ACCESS_URL` |
| Use next | AI functions on these files (Module 13) |
